I see. `bcf_hdr_parse_line` for the `##fileformat` line returns `*len = q - line + (*q ? 1 : 0)`. So it includes the `\n`. 

Now, in `bcf_hdr_parse`, after parsing the `##fileformat` line, `p += len`. Then it tries to parse the next line. The next line is `#CHROM...`. But `bcf_hdr_parse_line` returns NULL for lines that don't start with `##` (it checks `p[0] != '#' || p[1] != '#'`). So for the `#CHROM` line, it returns NULL with `*len = 0`.

Then in `bcf_hdr_parse`:
```c
while (NULL != (hrec = bcf_hdr_parse_line(hdr, p, &len))) {
    ...
    p += len;
}
assert(hrec == NULL);
if (len < 0) { ... }
else if (len > 0) { ... }
```

Since `len = 0` for the `#CHROM` line, it doesn't increment `p`. Then it checks `strncmp("#CHROM\tPOS", p, 10)`. This matches, so `done = 1`.

Then `bcf_hdr_parse_sample_line(hdr, p)` parses the sample line. This doesn't consume from the file.

So the record should start at byte 69. But the shared data is shifted by one byte.

}
